name: StarCraft
strap: Pick a campaign. Learn the war through its people.
description: Where to start StarCraft, why each entry point works, what to skip, and the lore and characters worth knowing.
intro: StarCraft’s story is a chain of betrayals, loyalties, and competing perspectives. The campaigns teach their armies, so you can begin without multiplayer expertise.
recommendation: Start Wings of Liberty for the most accessible campaign introduction. Choose StarCraft and Brood War, through Remastered, if you want Kerrigan and Raynor’s full original story.
basics: Human colonies, the zerg, and the protoss fight over a region far from Earth.
Terrans, zerg, and protoss have different institutions and motives. Their campaigns are sequential viewpoints on a shared conflict.
A comfortable setting lets you learn strategy without ranked-play expectations. Challenge modes and co-op commanders are optional.

entries.title: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
entries.audience: I want the easiest campaign introduction
entries.why: Raynor’s ship, crew, and mission choices give the conflict a human centre. Tutorials teach the army as the story grows.
entries.need: Raynor leads rebels against Mengsk; his history with Kerrigan makes the zerg threat personal.
entries.skip: A full original-game playthrough, Brood War, multiplayer, and novels.
entries.tradeoff: The starting situation contains major original-story developments. Read the short recap if you accept those spoilers.
entries.next: Continue to Heart of the Swarm, then Whispers of Oblivion and Legacy of the Void.

entries.title: StarCraft / Remastered
entries.audience: I want the original betrayals and relationships
entries.why: The terran, zerg, and protoss campaigns establish the people whose choices drive both games. Remastered includes the original and Brood War stories.
entries.need: The sector’s human government faces rebellion and alien threats.
entries.skip: StarCraft II, books, competitive build orders, and perfect mission scores.
entries.tradeoff: Older pathfinding and controls require patience. Play the campaign episodes in their intended sequence.
entries.next: Continue directly to Brood War, then Wings of Liberty.

entries.title: Legacy of the Void
entries.audience: I want to lead the protoss
entries.why: Artanis’s coalition has a clear immediate purpose, and its army offers a different style of strategy.
entries.need: The protoss seek to reclaim their home while a larger threat manipulates the conflict.
entries.skip: A full three-army marathon if the protoss are what brought you here.
entries.tradeoff: This is the saga’s concluding campaign, so its recap and epilogue reveal much of the earlier story.
entries.next: Play Whispers of Oblivion first; use earlier recaps if desired, then the main campaign and epilogue.

events.title: StarCraft
events.premise: Rebellion, alien invasion, and competing commands pull the sector into war.
events.recap: Mengsk abandons Kerrigan to the zerg and forms the Dominion. Kerrigan emerges transformed, while the protoss sacrifice Aiur’s Overmind victory at enormous cost.
events.why: Original foundation; play terran, zerg, then protoss episodes.

events.title: Brood War
events.premise: The protoss, invading UED, and zerg factions contest the broken balance of power.
events.recap: Kerrigan manipulates allies and rivals to consolidate the Swarm. The UED expedition is defeated, and her victory leaves Raynor with deeply personal reasons to oppose her.
events.why: Original saga continuation; episode order matters.

events.title: Wings of Liberty
events.premise: Raynor’s crew fights Dominion authority while pursuing artefacts connected to Kerrigan.
events.recap: The artefact strips away Kerrigan’s zerg form. Tychus’s hidden order to kill her forces Raynor to choose between the mission’s bargain and the person he wants to save.
events.why: Recommended accessible beginning with an optional earlier recap.

events.title: Heart of the Swarm
events.premise: Kerrigan gathers the Swarm while seeking answers about Raynor and revenge against Mengsk.
events.recap: Kerrigan becomes a primal zerg leader and overthrows Mengsk, while a larger cosmic conflict takes precedence over revenge.

events.title: Whispers of Oblivion
events.premise: Zeratul follows clues to a threat behind the sector’s wars.
events.recap: The missions connect the xel’naga prophecy to Amon’s plans and warn the protoss of the danger ahead.

events.title: Legacy of the Void
events.premise: Protoss communities must overcome division to confront Amon.
events.recap: The protoss sever Amon’s hold through the Khala and assemble a coalition to retake their future. The main campaign hands the saga to its epilogue.
events.why: Conclusion-focused alternative entry; stronger after the other campaigns.

events.title: Into the Void
events.premise: The three peoples confront the threat beyond their earlier wars.
events.recap: Kerrigan takes on xel’naga power and defeats Amon. The epilogue resolves the main saga’s cosmic conflict while leaving the peoples to their own futures.
events.why: Play after Legacy, not as a separate starting point.

events.title: Nova Covert Ops
events.premise: A Dominion ghost investigates covert operations and a threat within human politics.
events.recap: Nova confronts the Defenders of Man conspiracy rather than restarting the main xel’naga saga.

characters.name: Jim Raynor
characters.motivation: He wants his resistance to stand for people rather than another ruler’s ambition.
characters.relationships: Kerrigan and Mengsk turn political conflict into personal betrayal.

characters.name: Sarah Kerrigan
characters.role: A terran ghost at the story’s beginning
characters.motivation: Control over her own life becomes inseparable from power over others.
characters.relationships: Raynor and Mengsk define competing parts of her history.

updates.text: Mengsk’s abandonment leads to her transformation by the zerg.

characters.name: Arcturus Mengsk
characters.motivation: His pursuit of victory tests how far political liberation can turn into personal rule.
characters.relationships: Raynor and Kerrigan know the human cost of his plans.

updates.text: The rebellion installs him at the head of the Dominion.

characters.name: Zeratul
characters.motivation: He seeks knowledge dangerous enough to change the fate of his people.
characters.relationships: Tassadar and Artanis connect his work to a divided protoss society.

characters.name: Tassadar
characters.motivation: He challenges inherited divisions when survival demands cooperation.
characters.relationships: Zeratul and Raynor become unlikely allies.

updates.text: His sacrifice destroys the Overmind on Aiur.

characters.name: Artanis
characters.motivation: He tries to build a shared future from communities divided by history.
characters.relationships: Zeratul’s warnings help change how he understands duty.

characters.name: Tychus Findlay
characters.motivation: A bargain for freedom places him inside a mission with hidden demands.
characters.relationships: His history with Raynor complicates the campaign’s trust.

updates.text: His order to kill Kerrigan puts him in direct conflict with Raynor.

characters.name: Nova Terra
characters.motivation: She must decide which orders serve the people they claim to protect.
characters.relationships: Dominion institutions give her mission its political stakes.

factions: The Confederacy, Dominion, UED, and rebels have different interests. “Terran” is a species grouping, not one faction.
Zerg leadership and purpose change across the campaigns; Kerrigan is not their only historical authority.
Aiur’s templar and the dark templar carry old divisions; Artanis’s project seeks cooperation beyond them.
Ancient creators and their legacy connect the local wars to the saga’s larger threat.
timeline_help: Campaign release order broadly follows the story. Play each original game’s episodes in sequence. Whispers is a prologue and Into the Void an epilogue, not extra full games. The starting-route filter marks the central saga; Wings of Liberty remains a valid shorter starting commitment.
scope: Covers StarCraft, Brood War, the three StarCraft II campaigns, Whispers of Oblivion, Into the Void, and Nova Covert Ops. Remastered is a version of the original campaigns. Nova is optional follow-up content. Multiplayer, co-op commander lore, books, and the unreleased StarCraft: Ghost are not required.
